open_points.subject: Project
open_points.question: What is a project in this service, is it a value or entity, who mints its identity, and is that identity the Client Portal project identity or a deliverer-local identity?
options: A Project entity identified by an existing Client Portal project ID
A deliverer-local Project entity mapped to a Client Portal project
No Project model; operations receive an opaque project identifier
open_points.default_guess: Use an entity whose identity is the existing Client Portal project ID.

witness.initial: A Portal project exists and has a synchronized folder.
events: The kernel asks the deliverer to scan using a project reference.
The deliverer resolves the folder and later records publication against the Portal store.
outcomes: The reference is the Portal project ID and directly identifies the project in both systems.
The reference is a deliverer-local ID that must first be mapped to a Portal project.
witness.observer: The kernel and the deliverer repository implementation

open_points.subject: project token
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token
open_points.question: What model the token represents, whether it is a value or entity, who mints it and from what, and whether it is uniquely bound to one project are not defined.
options: An opaque value minted per project by the deliverer
An entity minted and stored by the deliverer with lifecycle such as active or revoked
A Portal-minted credential passed through to the deliverer
A single service token accompanied by a separate project ID
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an opaque deliverer-minted value uniquely bound to one project.

witness.initial: Projects A and B exist and the kernel holds a token obtained for A.
events: The kernel invokes scan for project B with A's token.
outcomes: The token is project-bound, so the operation is rejected.
The token authenticates the caller generally, so the operation may scan B.
witness.observer: The kernel and the owner of project B

open_points.subject: project token and deliverer credential
open_points.question: Is the deliverer's HTTPS credential a model distinct from the per-project token, and which actor mints and owns each credential?
options: Two distinct values: a deployment-managed service credential plus a deliverer-managed project token
The HTTPS credential is also the project token
The service credential identifies the kernel while the project token is a Portal-issued project capability
open_points.default_guess: Model them as distinct values: deployment owns the service credential and the deliverer owns a project-bound token.

witness.initial: The HTTPS route is installed and the kernel has the deliverer's credential but no project token.
events: The kernel invokes scan for a project using only the HTTPS credential.
outcomes: The request is authenticated at the route but fails because the separate project token is absent.
The HTTPS credential is the token, so the project operation proceeds.

open_points.subject: project folder
open_points.text: only a confirmed folder is used
open_points.question: What model owns folder identity and the confirmed state, who establishes that identity and confirmation, and which product action creates or changes the confirmation?
options: A Folder entity with a confirmation status changed by an administrative action
A Project entity containing an immutable confirmed-folder reference
A configuration value supplied by deployment, with no runtime folder entity
Confirmation is derived on every scan from filesystem state
open_points.default_guess: Use a Folder entity mapped to a project, with an explicit confirmation status set by an administrative action.

witness.initial: A project has two Syncthing directories, one previously used and one newly synchronized.
events: An operator associates the new directory with the project.
outcomes: Association alone makes the directory confirmed, so the scan reads it.
Confirmation is a separate state transition, so the scan continues to use the old directory or refuses to scan.

open_points.subject: source photo
open_points.question: What identifies the source photo, whether it is a value or entity, who mints that identity, and whether renames, moves, or identical bytes denote the same photo?
options: An entity identified by project plus stable relative path
A value identified by a content hash
An entity with a deliverer-minted ID created during scan
A filesystem entry identified by inode or equivalent filesystem identity
open_points.default_guess: Create a deliverer-minted entity during scan and retain its project, path, and content fingerprint as facts.

witness.initial: A photo is scanned at one name and is then renamed without changing its bytes.
events: The kernel asks to scan again.
The kernel asks to deliver the discovered photo.
outcomes: The renamed entry is the same photo and retains its delivery history.
The renamed entry is a new photo and can produce a second delivery.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing hidden Portal photos

open_points.subject: delivered photo and source photo
open_points.question: Is a delivered photo the source Photo entity in a later lifecycle state, or a distinct Portal-side entity created from the source photo, and who mints its identity?
options: One Photo entity changes from discovered to delivered and stores a Portal object ID
A distinct DeliveredPhoto entity is minted by the deliverer from a SourcePhoto
A Portal media entity is minted by the Portal store and linked to a source-photo value
open_points.default_guess: Use a distinct delivered-photo entity linked to the source photo and identified by the Portal-side object ID.

witness.initial: A source photo has been discovered but not delivered.
events: The kernel invokes deliver one photo.
The deliverer strips metadata and writes the hidden photo to the Portal store.
outcomes: The existing Photo entity changes status and gains Portal facts.
A new DeliveredPhoto or Portal-media entity is created while the source Photo remains unchanged.
witness.observer: The kernel reading the delivery result and the owner viewing the Portal

open_points.subject: delivery identity
open_points.text: a repeated delivery creates nothing new
open_points.question: Which model represents a delivery, what makes two delivery attempts the same, and from which facts its identity or idempotency identity is minted are not defined.
options: One Delivery entity per source-photo identity
One Delivery entity per project and content hash
No Delivery entity; the delivered Portal photo is uniquely keyed by the source-photo identity
The caller supplies an idempotency identity
open_points.default_guess: Use one Delivery entity per project and source-photo identity, minted on the first successful delivery.

witness.initial: A source photo was delivered successfully and the kernel did not receive the response.
events: The kernel repeats deliver for the same source photo.
The deliverer checks existing state and returns a result.
outcomes: The existing delivery and hidden Portal photo are returned.
A second delivery is considered distinct because the retry has no shared identity and another hidden photo is created.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing hidden photos and the kernel

open_points.subject: publication
open_points.question: Does recording publication create a Publication entity, change a DeliveredPhoto or Delivery status, or both; who supplies or mints the publication identity; and which Portal action is the authoritative publication event?
options: Create an immutable Publication entity after the Portal show operation
Change DeliveredPhoto status from hidden to published
Change Delivery status and retain publication time as fields
Record a caller assertion without reading or linking to a Portal publication event
open_points.default_guess: Create an immutable Publication entity linked to the delivered photo after the Portal show operation is confirmed.

witness.initial: A delivered photo exists hidden in the Portal.
events: The owner uses the Portal operation to show the photo to the client.
The kernel invokes record its publication twice.
outcomes: One Publication entity is created and the repeat returns that same entity.
No publication entity exists; the delivered photo merely remains in a published status after both calls.
witness.observer: The kernel and any later reader of publication history

open_points.subject: delivered photo lifecycle
open_points.text: The owner reviews a delivered photo and shows it to the client with the Portal's own operation.
open_points.question: Which lifecycle statuses exist for the delivered photo, which system owns them, and whether the Portal show operation or the deliverer's record-publication operation performs the transition to published are not defined.
options: The Portal owns hidden and visible status; record publication only mirrors the completed transition
The deliverer owns delivered and published status; record publication performs the transition after the Portal action
Both systems hold statuses with an explicitly defined synchronization relationship
open_points.default_guess: The Portal owns visibility, while the deliverer records a separate publication fact only after the Portal operation succeeds.

events: The owner successfully shows it through the Portal.
Before record publication is called, the kernel reads the deliverer's state.
outcomes: The photo is already published because the Portal operation is authoritative.
The deliverer's model still says delivered or hidden until record publication changes it.
